A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T3-Unlearning study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original TOFU experiments with Llama 3.1 8B, computational efficiency measurements, and Gaussian-mixture simulations in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TOFU results, efficiency measurements, Gaussian-mixture simulations, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The frozen base model, regularized classifier training, low-rank classifier head, and temper-then-tilt inference rule are unchanged. Section 2 clarifies the probabilistic formulation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use TOFU with 5% and 10% author-forgetting splits, retained authors, Real Authors and World Facts evaluations, and the same univariate Gaussian-mixture scenarios in Appendix E.

E2.justification: The TOFU comparisons retain GradAscent, GradDiff, WGA, SatImp, UnDIAL, RMU, ULD, IdkDPO, NPO, and SimNPO. Changing UNDIAL to UnDIAL in the tables standardizes capitalization; no comparator is added, removed, or substantively revised.

E3.justification: The model, splits, metrics, greedy decoding, hyperparameter selection criterion, search grids, selected configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix F.3.3 describes the same temperature experiment more clearly.

E4.justification: Both retain the Gaussian sharpness and sample-size analyses, classifier and density examples in Figures 2–5, and TOFU temperature sensitivity in Table 5. Calling the latter an ablation study in v2 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both report five-seed TOFU averages and individual seed results, with seeds 1 and 2 used for tuning. Appendix E retains its 10-trial regularization search and 200-trial averaging; uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the plotted results in Figures 2–5 are unchanged. For example, T3-Unlearning's Forget Quality remains 0.914 and 0.671 on the 5% and 10% splits, respectively, with MU-ROUGE of 0.900 and 0.899.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the retain-support labels and integration domains in Appendix A.3, inserts the missing 1/n in Appendix D's population-proportion equation, and restores a missing square-root-of-tau factor in Appendix E's Gaussian integral. Section 2.1 also resolves inconsistent scaling of the optimal classifier. The main theorem statements and rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction removes v1's claim that tempering improves dependence on classifier excess risk, retaining the tradeoff between tempering bias and robustness to concentrated forget distributions. The abstract and principal method, guarantee, and empirical superiority claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly explains that retain and forget distributions can overlap, so unlearning may require probability adjustment rather than hard exclusion. Appendix D replaces an 'unbiased' estimator claim with 'asymptotically consistent,' qualifying the same estimator more accurately.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility information is retained, including feature caching, classifier dimensions, hyperparameters, NVIDIA GH200 hardware, AdamW, scheduling, batch sizes, and ZeRO settings. No substantive code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds 'Ascent Fails to Forget' by Mavrothalassitis and colleagues [MPLC26], citing failure guarantees for ascent-style objectives when positioning T3-Unlearning. The remaining cited works and overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands and reorganizes Section 2's probabilistic explanation, distinguishes random variables from their realizations, and makes local prose and terminology corrections throughout the main text and proofs. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects the classifier output domain from real-valued vectors to [0,1]-valued vectors and updates conditional-probability notation. Tables change placement relative to surrounding prose, and some equations are reformatted; all five figures and five tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical accuracy and clarity through the support, normalization, and Gaussian-factor corrections in Appendices A.3, D, and E. Removing the misleading excess-risk claim and qualifying the estimator as asymptotically consistent also reduce inconsistencies. These are useful local improvements; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
